title: ERCOT Analysis
text:
ERCOT is a wholesale electricity provider in Texas and operate four geographical load zones, Houston, North, South, and West. Real-Time Co‑Optimization plus Batteries(RTCB) is a co-opimization and battery system that was intergrated by ERCOT in December 2025. RTCB was intergrated to improve reliablity, efficiency, and responsiveness. These graphs are looking into the affects of RTCB intergration on ERCOT’s loads zones by looking into the maximum price spread between the four loading zones.
The first graph shows the number of extreme price spreads by month. An extreme price spread is defined as a price spread between load zones that is in the 95th percentile of Pre-RTCB price spreads. The graph shows That Post-RTCB tends to have less extreme price spreads.









This next graph shows the median price spread by the hour of the day. The median spread Pre-RTCB is higher than Post-RTCB before 12:00 but lower after. This could show the RTCB’s affect on efficiently storing energy through out the day.









This next three graphs show the Western load zone’s median price difference compared to the other three load zones in ERCOT. One trend that emerges from the plots is that Post-RTCB tends to have lower price difference between load zones with the exception of the Houston load zone, which is more volitile.
